text: The following question stood in the name of Dr Lim Wee Kiak – 44 To ask the Minister for Health (a) how many instances of non-compliance of telemedicine guidelines have been reported to or identified by the Ministry in the past year given the recent findings of potential lapses in telehealth consultations; (b) what are the primary reasons for these lapses; (c) what steps have been taken to minimise such lapses; and (d) whether there is a protocol for patients to seek support and advice if they have concerns and wish to report a telehealth consultation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in light of the revocation of MaNaDr Clinic’s licence to provide outpatient medical services, whether the Ministry has observed any similar trends of unethical telemedicine practices by licensed providers of outpatient medical services, particularly of short consultations; (b) whether there is any evidence of misuse in the dispensation of drugs in this case; and (c) what other penalties or disciplinary actions have been imposed on the licensed medical practitioners associated with the clinic.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in the last year, how many medical clinics providing teleconsultations have been audited or investigated for irregularities; (b) of these, how many clinics have been issued warnings or subject to more severe penalties; and (c) what are the common irregularities committed by such clinics.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In addition, medical practitioners have also been referred to the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) for potential lapses in professional standards.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is important to recognise that telemedicine can bring tremendous benefits to patients, especially those who are immobile or doing regular follow-ups.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It makes healthcare much more accessible and convenient to our patients.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, as in any new service delivery model, there will be potential for abuse and misuse, especially in the initial period of implementation.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: MOH will take the necessary enforcement actions so that, over time, best practices become normalised.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the meantime, the public should raise concerns regarding the provision of telemedicine to MOH via the public feedback channels available on the Ministry’s website.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State also elaborate whether MOH can name the other two companies that provided telemedicine and where action has been taken, and for the remaining five, what is the status of the investigation?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The second question is, how many cases were there where the telemedicine consultations lasted less than a minute?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And finally, whether there were cases where there were actually no patients, but they have recorded that there were patients?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The first question is that the Senior Minister of State said three companies were investigated and actions were taken for their lapses.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: We know that one or two have been mentioned in the press.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second part is of the remaining five that were investigated, what was the status of the investigations?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are a number of licensees involved and, indeed, there were some very short teleconsultations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As I said, the investigations are still ongoing, so we are trying to establish the exact number.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A short teleconsultation is not automatically incorrect, if it is a regular patient, if it is a follow-up, if the necessary information has been obtained.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I think we have to look at the entire clinical care that has been provided and make sure it is appropriate.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is not the fact of telemedicine that is necessarily the problem.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is whether correct clinical care has been provided through this modality and that sometimes requires an inpatient consultation, sometimes it requires the appropriate breadth and time for the interaction so that the correct information is provided, and, in some cases, it is an issue of whether or not the correct documentation of the process has been carried out.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, all of these things are part of the investigation process.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Senior Minister of State has shared that eight telemedicine providers are under investigation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is just to get a feel of what is the percentage of the providers that are under investigation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Second, some of my residents in Pasir Ris have brought up that the contacts of telemedicine clinics have been shared as a means to get easy medical certificates.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In fact, a concerned parent shared that some students are using this as a means to avoid taking tests.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, how do we monitor that this modern convenience of telemedicine services is not abused?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And how do we then proactively monitor it?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What are the avenues for us to report such cases?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, that is the number that we are dealing with.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of it is through the professional route and some of it is through public complaints.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Ultimately, has a correct assessment been provided and is the treatment, whether it is medication, investigation or a medical certificate, appropriate to the clinical condition that has been detected and appropriately documented?
